newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain will meet its 1997 deficit goal - Rato.
newsitem.headline: Spain will meet its 1997 deficit goal - Rato.

text.p: Spanish Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said on Wednesday that Spain would take every step necessary to ensure it fulfills its 1997 public deficit target of three percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
He added that the credibility of the 1997 objective and its fulfilment had increased now that Spain had met the 1996 goal of 4.4 percent to GDP.

"The government is conscious that the meeting of the 1997 deficit target is a fundamental part of our economic commitment...So the government has adopted measures to keep public expenditure under control...and it could adopt measures to rule out any overshooting," he told an economic seminar.
Rato added that the government, in its first meeting of the year with regional authorities, had taken an important first step to getting regional expenditures under control.
He said the will to fulfill the European Stability pact agreed to in Dublin is shared by the Spanish regional government.

In 1997, the public deficit corresponding to the regions is a mere 0.2 percent of the total three percent target of the public deficit. In 1996, that figure was expected to have been around 0.4-0.5 percent.
Rato said Spain is expected to see solid economic growth from the second half of the year with a pick-up in demand, continued control of public expenditure and moderating inflation.
